newsitem.title: DUBAI: Rabbani says regrouping to move against Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Rabbani says regrouping to move against Taleban.

text.p: Ousted Afghan president Burhanuddin Rabbani told Iranian television his government was regrouping in northern Afghanistan to move against the Islamic Taleban militia, which captured Kabul last month.

The television said on Monday night Rabbani told its correspondent in Afghanistan that a form of high state council and a cabinet had been set up and "once a more complete council had been formed, the government would move against Taleban".

"He (Rabbani) said the present aim of his government was to gather all groups who wanted to struggle against foreign aggression, and to unite them," said the television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

It quoted Rabbani as saying he met a representative of Uzbek strongman General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls six northern Afghan provinces, on Sunday and Monday "and the results would be announced very soon."
Dostum has vowed to fight to prevent further advances by Taleban forces, which captured Kabul on September 27, into northern Afghanistan.

Taleban's ultra-conservative interpretation of Islam and its Pashtun ethnic flavour have rung alarm bells throughout northern Afghanistan, especially among Uzbeks and Tajiks whose military leaders were at odds until recently.
Dostum and Ahmad Shah Masood, Rabbani's top military commander whose government forces were routed from Kabul by Taleban, appoear ready to cooperate against what they see as a common threat.
